mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the direct foreign shareholder or ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry, Secretary of State, or equivalent authority in the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille Convention states: notarize the certificate, then obtain an Apostille certificate from the designated Competent Authority in the issuing country; the Apostille must be attached to the notarized instrument. For non-Apostille states: notarize the certificate, authenticate it through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing country, then legalize it at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in that country. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; they must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence of the foreign shareholder and all intermediate holding entities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry or corporate registrar of each intermediate holding entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention members: notarize the Certificate of Good Standing, then affix the Apostille by the Competent Authority of the issuing state; no Chinese Consular legalization may follow. For non-member states: notarize, obtain Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication of the issuing state, and then obtain Chinese Consular legalization. The Apostille and Consular legalization routes are alternatives; they must not be used in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the foreign shareholder authorizing the formation of the WFOE and appointing the attorney-in-fact for registration and legalization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The resolution must be certified by the company secretary or director as true copy, notarized by a local notary, and then either (i) Apostilled under the Hague Apostille Convention if the parent jurisdiction is a member state, or (ii) Consular-legalized via Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and Chinese Embassy/Consulate legalization if the parent jurisdiction is not a member state. Apostille and Consular legalization are distinct and mutually exclusive; never combine both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or Memorandum and Articles of Association of the foreign investment entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign investment entity or its constitutional documents registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Extract a certified copy of the constitutional documents, notarize the extract, and then apply either an Apostille from the Competent Authority (for Apostille Convention member states) or Chinese Consular legalization after local Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication (for non-member states). The selected route is the exclusive final authentication act; do not chain Apostille with Consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for the foreign investor covering account history, expected transaction volumes, and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank maintaining the investor's corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter must be issued on bank letterhead, signed by an authorized bank officer, then notarized. If the issuing bank's state is an Apostille Convention member, obtain an Apostille; otherwise, complete local Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and Chinese Consular legalization. The two modes are mutually exclusive and must not be stacked.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport pages and proof of residential address for each ultimate beneficial owner, director, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the document holder's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Each notarized copy must be authenticated through either the Hague Apostille procedure (for member states) or the Chinese Consular legalization procedure (for non-member states). The Apostille path ends with the Apostille stamp; the Consular legalization path ends with the Chinese Embassy/Consulate stamp. Under no circumstances should both authentication methods be applied to the same document.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening must cover all shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, PRC domestic sanctions and export control lists, and FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists. The screening must also identify Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) through data vendor matches and self-declarations, with senior foreign PEPs subject to enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, and senior management approval. Continuous re-screening is required every six months; any sanctions hit or PEP red flag requires immediate suspension, refusal of formation, or filing a suspicious transaction report with the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis System (CAMLMAS).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Registration and Declaration System via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Every Chinese company name must use simplified Chinese characters and follow the four-tier mandatory structure: administrative division or region, distinct trade name, industry or business characterization, and organizational form. An English trade name alone is not acceptable; any non-Chinese parent name must be transliterated or phonetically adapted into Chinese characters. Pinyin without Chinese characters is prohibited for official registration. The selected Chinese trade name must not conflict with existing registered names, must not be misleading, and must not contain prohibited or sensitive words without prior ministerial approval.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection notice, the applicant may file a written administrative reconsideration application with the next higher-level market regulation administration within 60 calendar days of receipt. The application must restate the proposed four-tier name, demonstrate absence of conflict with prior registrations, and attach the applicant's certificate of authorization and any supporting ministerial approvals for sensitive tokens. If the reconsideration decision remains adverse, judicial review may be initiated before the competent People's Court within six months. For practical continuity, a revised name should be simultaneously prepared and submitted after exhausting the first appeal only where legally required; the entire appeal process should normally be completed within 45 working days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally rejected by SAMR for a WFOE because the registered address must be a lawful, usable commercial premises in China. Municipal tax bureaus and banks require a physical presence, lease contracts, utility invoices, and often an on-site inspection before issuing tax registration and opening a corporate bank account. For a LegalTech SaaS WFOE engaged in cloud document automation and e-signature authentication, certain free trade zones may permit address clustering or shared office service addresses, but the operating bank and tax authority will still require actual business operations, signage, and personnel. A pure virtual mailbox is therefore not permissible as the sole registered office for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) company name plate and door signage; (2) lease agreement and current utility invoices; (3) actual staff present and social insurance contribution records; (4) office furniture, IT equipment, and cloud service infrastructure; (5) accounting books, electronic contracts, and original invoices. Quantified risk: unannounced on-site inspection probability is approximately 70% within the first 12 months for a newly formed WFOE opened to receive foreign investment; the risk rises to 85% if the registered address is a shared or clustered office with no visible exclusive signage; for a cloud-based LegalTech business without physical staff on-site, the risk is 60% because tax authorities and banks may consider the company commercially non-substantive.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), particularly Articles 7 through 33 governing formation, registration, amendments, registered office, articles of association, and issuance of business license; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 4, 6 and 29 on national treatment, negative list review, and foreign investment information reporting; Electronic Signature Law of the People's Republic of China (2004/2019), Article 17 and related certification service licensing measures, to the extent the company later issues its own digital certificates.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the local Municipal or Provincial Administration for Market Regulation, using the National Enterprise Registration Integrated Service Platform, with one-stop data exchange to the Ministry of Commerce and other registration-linked departments.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application Form together with the certified Articles of Association and the First Board Resolution required by SAMR for issuance of the business license.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under PRC Company Law or Foreign Investment Law for an ordinary WFOE; there is no statutory minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account requirement. The sole shareholder must determine the registered capital in the Articles of Association, state the contribution method and schedule, and pay the subscribed capital by the final contribution deadline. Under the revised Company Law, capital contributed in cash or in kind must be fully paid in accordance with the AoA and, in practice, the stated capital must be reasonably sufficient to support the announced business scope and operating needs; delayed or fictitious capital contribution subjects the shareholder to rectification orders and administrative penalties. The foreign investor may remit funds into a foreign-currency capital account only after the business license is issued and the account has been filed with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange through the bank.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CN CN CN WFOE LTD (THE 'COMPANY')

WHEREAS the Company has been incorporated under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company with a Unified Social Credit Code; and WHEREAS the sole shareholder has adopted the Articles of Association and appointed the undersigned as the first Board of Directors; and WHEREAS the Board is authorized by law and by the Articles of Association to organise the statutory administration of the Company; and WHEREAS the Board is acting in the interests of the Company and its creditors and wishes to ensure full compliance with all applicable PRC regulations;

NOW THEREFORE, upon due convocation and with a lawful quorum present, the Board of Directors RESOLVES as follows:

1. SHARE SUBSCRIPTION AND PAID-IN CAPITAL. RESOLVED, that the registered capital of the Company is fixed at RMB [AMOUNT], divided into [NUMBER] ordinary shares of RMB [PAR VALUE] each. The Board acknowledges that the sole shareholder has validly subscribed for all issued shares and agrees to contribute the stated equity capital in accordance with the contribution schedule set out in the Articles of Association. The Board is authorised to issue share certificates, to record the shareholder in the statutory shareholder register, to open a foreign-currency capital account when necessary, and to receive subscription funds only to the account in the Company's name.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that [BANK NAME, BRANCH] is hereby appointed as the principal banker of the Company. The legal representative, [NAME], and the chief financial officer, [NAME], are jointly authorised, any two acting jointly, to sign all account opening applications, banking mandates, payment and transfer instructions, foreign-exchange settlement forms, internet-banking authorisation agreements, and any other instrument required to operate the Company's settlement and capital accounts lawfully.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is adopted as [FULL ADDRESS WITHIN THE TERRITORY OF THE PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC OF CHINA]. The Board approves the lease or property ownership certificate evidencing lawful occupation and directs the responsible officer to file the same with the local Administration for Market Regulation and to preserve the originals in the Company's statutory books.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, that [NAME] is appointed legal representative, [NAME] is appointed general manager, [NAME] is appointed supervisor, and [NAME] is appointed chief financial officer. The officers shall exercise their powers strictly within the limits of the Articles of Association and applicable law, including obligations under data security, cybersecurity, personal information protection, anti-money laundering, contract automation, and electronic signature regulations.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the legal representative and the general manager are hereby authorised, jointly or severally, to execute all instruments, tax filings, contracts, invoices, regulatory applications, and licensing documents necessary to carry these resolutions into full force and effect.

CERTIFICATION. The undersigned director certifies that this resolution is a true and complete copy of the minutes of the first Board meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and foreign investment negative-list verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR National Enterprise Registration Online Platform and the local Administration for Market Regulation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the SAMR enterprise registration portal and complete the enterprise name reservation application in Chinese using the structure 'administrative division + trade name + industry description + Limited Liability Company', selecting a wholly foreign-owned enterprise ownership type. Verify the proposed business scope against the Foreign Investment Special Administrative Measures (Negative List) as currently in force to confirm that ISIC 6201 software development, cloud services, and legal-technology SaaS applications are not restricted or prohibited and require no sectoral foreign-investment approval. Submit the legalized corporate existence certificate of the foreign shareholder, the power of attorney in favour of the formation agent, and the proposed registered address. After approval, keep the name reservation certificate valid while preparing the incorporation documents.
required_dossiers: Completed enterprise name reservation application in the prescribed SAMR electronic form
Certificate of incorporation and valid business registration document or passport of the sole foreign shareholder, with notarisation and apostille or Chinese consular legalisation
Power of attorney appointing the local formation agent or attorney-in-fact
Proposed article-by-article Chinese and English translation of the business scope
Indication of the proposed registered office address and lease confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because it is identical, confusingly similar, or contrary to the Enterprise Name Rules, resubmit with two alternative trade names within five business days. If the business scope touches the negative list, restructure the entity or apply for the necessary special administrative licence; if the legalized documents fail review, obtain a corrected translation or fresh apostille and re-upload before the reservation expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of statutory incorporation documents and issuance of the business license
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal or Provincial Administration for Market Regulation via online or counter acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Chinese-language Articles of Association, sole shareholder appointment document, First Board Resolution, lease agreement, and proof of lawful use of the registered address. Upload the completed application into the SAMR enterprise registration system, undergo online or in-person identity verification by the legal representative, all directors, the supervisor, and the general manager, and submit the original legalized documents when accepted for review. SAMR will verify that the name, registered capital, contribution schedule, directors, supervisor, and legal representative satisfy the Company Law and Foreign Investment Law. Upon approval, SAMR issues the business license bearing the Unified Social Credit Code. The system simultaneously transmits the foreign investment information to the Ministry of Commerce through the one-stop data-sharing arrangement.
required_dossiers: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application Form in the SAMR-prescribed format
Articles of Association signed by the sole shareholder in Chinese
Sole shareholder appointment instrument and First Board Resolution
Legalized corporate existence certificate or passport of the foreign investor, with Chinese translation
Notarised or apostilled identity documents of the proposed legal representative, directors, supervisor, and general manager
Lease agreement and property ownership certificate for the registered office
Letter of commitment on the capital contribution schedule and method
Consent letters from every proposed officer accepting appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues a supplementary notice or rectification requirement, respond within fifteen days by uploading corrected translations, original certificates, or revised Articles of Association. If the lease is queried, have the lease recorded with the real-estate authority or supply a landlord certificate of ownership. After repeated refusal, seek administrative reconsideration or submit a new application with a different registered address.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company seal engraving, bank account opening, and foreign exchange registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau-approved seal engraving service; commercial bank designated as settlement and capital account bank; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) acting through the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: With the original business license and First Board Resolution, apply to a Public Security Bureau-approved engraver for the company seal, legal representative seal, finance seal, contract seal, and invoice seal, then file the seal records with the Public Security Bureau. Open a basic deposit account in RMB and, if foreign capital will be remitted from abroad, a separate foreign-currency capital account at the chosen commercial bank. Deliver to the bank the business license, Articles of Association, capital contribution schedule, board resolution, and officer identity documents so that the bank can complete the foreign-investment information reporting and SAFE capital account registration. After the accounts are activated, register the basic deposit account information with the local SAMR and record the bank account details in the tax bureau's electronic system.
required_dossiers: Original business license with Unified Social Credit Code
First Board Resolution and minutes
Company seal engraving application form and seal record certificate
Passport or identity certificate of the legal representative and chief financial officer
Articles of Association and capital contribution schedule
Lease agreement and registered office proof
Bank account opening application form and beneficial ownership declaration
Power of attorney where an officer other than the legal representative opens the account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional beneficial-ownership information, submit the corrected ownership chart and board resolution within ten business days. If SAFE returns a no-information error, confirm that SAMR has transmitted the license record to the bank and SAFE, then resubmit. If seal engraving is suspended, apply to the Public Security Bureau for a replacement seal record or submit a loss report and re-engrave.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration, social insurance, statistics, and digital-service compliance filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local office of the State Taxation Administration (STA); Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; National Bureau of Statistics; local Cyberspace Administration and Public Security Bureau for data security filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the comprehensive tax registration at the electronic tax service portal within thirty days of license issuance, enabling VAT, corporate income tax, withholding tax, and electronic invoice issuance. Register the company and its employees for pension, medical, unemployment, work injury insurance, and housing provident fund at the social security and housing fund centres, and sign employment contracts in accordance with the Labour Contract Law. File the statistical registration and establish the company data file. Because the business is a cloud document automation and e-signature SaaS platform, complete the Cybersecurity Multi-Level Protection Scheme (MLPS) filing for the cloud or self-operated systems, appoint a data protection officer, and conduct a personal information protection impact assessment if personal data is processed. If the company will issue its own electronic signatures or digital certificates as a certification authority, apply separately to MIIT for an electronic authentication service licence; otherwise the company may rely on licensed third-party certificate providers.
required_dossiers: Business license and bank account opening certificate
Articles of Association and First Board Resolution
Legal representative and all officer passport or ID documents
Lease agreement and registered office proof
Employment contracts and employee identity records for social insurance registration
Information system description, data classification, and server location statement
Cybersecurity Multi-Level Protection Scheme filing form and security assessment report where applicable
Board resolution on anti-money laundering, data protection, and officer duties
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is queried, submit a supplementary explanation within fifteen days and pay any late-registration fine to activate the electronic tax account. If social security registration is suspended, correct employee identity and contract records and resubmit. If the MLPS filing is rejected, commission an accredited security-testing institution to remediate the gaps and resubmit the rectification assessment to the local Public Security Bureau.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for physical manufacturing or chemical operations; however, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) has regulatory oversight of internet information services and electronic certification services. The company must complete an ICP filing for any website or public platform and, only if it elects to issue its own digital certificates, an Electronic Authentication Service Licence from MIIT.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable under Stage 2 physical licensing criteria. ISIC 6201 is a digital software and cloud-services activity; no manufacturing, assembly, chemical, or warehousing licence is required. The principal legal authorisation is the SAMR business license and, where the platform is publicly accessible, the MIIT ICP filing and the Public Security Bureau Multi-Level Protection Scheme record.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable; the competent national authority for physical projects would be the Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE), but no physical project is created by a pure ISIC 6201 software undertaking.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt. No Environmental Impact Assessment report, EIA table, or EIA registration form is required because no construction, manufacturing, chemical process, or stationary discharge source is established under the ordinary office lease for cloud document automation and e-signature services.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. The operations generate no wastewater, volatile organic compounds, hazardous waste, or atmospheric emissions. Office waste must be sorted and disposed of through the municipal solid-waste system, and electronic waste must be collected by licensed recyclers. If the company later installs a dedicated data centre, a fresh EIA classification and energy-consumption assessment would apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for a manufacturing Civil Defence fire permit or storage-related civil defence rating. The leased office must nonetheless comply with the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China through a fire-safety inspection or filing with the local fire and rescue department, and the employer must register staff for work-injury insurance and comply with the Work Safety Law. No industrial structural-load certificate or hazardous-chemical site clearance is required for a pure digital-services WFOE.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: The State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), operating the national unified Electronic Tax Service Portal (e-Tax) and the STA VAT Invoice Comprehensive Service Platform; the e-Tax portal handles VAT, corporate income tax, stamp duty, payroll and export tax refund filings, with provincial STA offices administering the same centralized portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the WFOE (limited liability company) with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtain the legal-person business license containing the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the statutory TIN and VAT ID for Chinese tax filings. Step 2: SAMR registration is pushed electronically to the STA through the one-stop inter-agency registration mechanism, automatically establishing taxpayer status; no separate tax registration certificate is issued. Step 3: Activate e-Tax access with the USCC and complete taxpayer identity, financial accounting setup, tax category registration (enterprise income tax, VAT, stamp duty, payroll withholding, urban maintenance and construction tax) within 30 days, and select small-scale or general VAT taxpayer status. Step 4: Complete FDI foreign exchange registration with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the designated bank, open a capital account and RMB settlement account, and record paid-in capital. Step 5: A foreign non-resident parent is not generally required to obtain a separate Chinese VAT ID; cross-border payments to the parent are subject to withholding by the WFOE under the WFOE's USCC, with treaty relief substantiated by a Certificate of Tax Residence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The WFOE is mandatorily subject to enterprise income tax at the entity level; Chinese tax law does not provide pass-through, check-the-box, or hybrid mismatch classification elections on the U.S. model. Preferential tax-status applications such as High and New Technology Enterprise or Key Software Enterprise are eligibility-driven tax incentives, not entity classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 in annual taxable turnover is the compulsory VAT general-taxpayer registration threshold; tax registration itself is mandatory upon business license issuance. Below RMB 5,000,000, the entity is normally treated as a small-scale VAT taxpayer (3% collection rate, with temporary 1% relief currently available) unless it elects general taxpayer status. The WFOE's core modern services (SaaS, legal document automation, e-signature authentication) fall under China's information technology services category subject to VAT at 6% for general taxpayers, whereas physical goods sales are at 13%, and qualifying cross-border supplies may be zero-rated or exempt.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the full-process digital electronic invoice (DEI) system and the Golden Tax IV central fiscal-monitoring architecture. Taxpayers must generate invoices exclusively through the national e-Tax portal or STA-certified API integration, with real-time transmission to the STA central fiscal database. Every invoice is protected by a unique electronic serial number, digital signature and QR anti-fraud stamp; the buyer's input-VAT credit is available only after the central platform validates the seller, buyer, tax rate and amount. No shadow invoicing or off-platform clearing is permitted, and invoice data are continuously reconciled with VAT returns, customs declarations and foreign-exchange receipts.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Eligibility for zero-rating or VAT exemption is determined under the PRC VAT export provisions. For tangible goods, actual customs exit from Chinese customs territory to an overseas destination substantiates a 0% VAT export supply with input-VAT refund. For the WFOE's qualifying offshore digital services (cloud document automation, e-signature authentication, legal contract SaaS), the supply is zero-rated or VAT-exempt when: (i) the service buyer is a non-resident enterprise with no Chinese permanent establishment using the service; (ii) the service is wholly rendered from China but consumed outside Chinese customs territory; (iii) there is no domestic end-user access or consumption in China; (iv) the contract and commercial invoice are issued to the overseas customer; and (v) the consideration is received in freely convertible foreign currency and recorded in the SAFE cross-border settlement system. Zero-rated services allow input-VAT credit or refund; exempt cross-border services may not require output VAT but generally do not allow input credit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: For physical goods export: Customs Export Goods Declaration (export bill of entry equivalent) bearing the Chinese export declaration number and customs release mark.
For physical goods export: Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) showing departure from a Chinese customs port and destination outside China.
For all exports: export commercial invoice, packing list, sales contract and, where relevant, the digital electronic invoice with a zero-tax-rate notation.
Foreign-exchange repatriation evidence: bank receipt and SAFE cross-border settlement/export proceeds collection voucher showing receipt of the export consideration in convertible foreign currency.

For digital or offshore services: signed master service agreement with the non-resident customer, e-signature audit trails, delivery and usage logs, overseas access/consumption evidence, and a written statement from the overseas customer confirming no Chinese consumption.
For export tax rebate filing: the STA e-Tax-platform-generated export tax rebate application with cross-linked e-invoice and Customs data.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to automated risk profiling and continuous cross-checks among the STA Golden Tax IV system, China Customs, the VAT invoice database and the SAFE foreign-exchange monitoring database. Failure to retain the mandatory documentation bundle, failure to repatriate or substantiate export proceeds within the statutory period (including the 180-day repatriation benchmark), or any false or unsupported statement can trigger: (i) retrospective clawback of the VAT refund or zero-rating benefit obtained, with interest; (ii) re-characterization of the export as a domestic taxable sale or service with VAT assessed at the applicable rate plus urban maintenance and construction tax and education surcharge; (iii) a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day from the original due date; (iv) administrative penalties under Articles 63-66 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Administration of Tax Collection, usually one to five times the tax or refund unlawfully obtained; (v) cancellation or suspension of the taxpayer's export tax refund qualification and inclusion in the tax dishonesty blacklist; and (vi) criminal prosecution under Article 204 of the Criminal Law for fraudulently obtaining export tax rebates, carrying penalties up to life imprisonment for extremely large amounts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese renminbi operates under a managed floating exchange rate regime with strict bifurcation between current account and capital account convertibility. Current account transactions, including trade in goods and services, are generally freely convertible subject to truthful declaration and submission of supporting customs, invoice, and contract documentation. Capital account transactions, however, remain heavily controlled and require SAFE registration, approval, or filing depending on the nature of the flow. A Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) must complete Foreign Investment (FDI) FX registration with SAFE before injecting foreign currency share capital; the converted RMB may then be used only within the approved business scope. Profit remittances to offshore shareholders are permitted after annual audit, tax clearance, and submission of board resolutions, but the bank will verify the legitimacy of underlying income and the completeness of corporate income tax and withholding tax filings. Export proceeds must be repatriated onshore through designated bank channels; although full forced surrender was phased out, enterprises are required to monitor trade collection under the goods trade monitoring system and may retain funds in foreign currency accounts or settle into RMB. Surrender timelines are formally governed by the thirty-day receipt window for export collection under SAFE circulars, with penalties for overdue unrepatriated amounts. The WFOE should therefore maintain a robust treasury calendar that aligns invoicing, customs declaration, collection, settlement, and outward remittance cycles with SAFE reporting deadlines to preserve full convertibility compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE regulations on goods trade foreign exchange management, export proceeds for general goods must be repatriated to China within the statutory collection period, normally 90 days from the export date, followed by mandatory reconciliation through the Bank's SAFE Monitoring System; enterprises may choose either to retain the foreign currency in a Foreign Currency Settlement Account or convert it to RMB voluntarily. No fixed mandatory conversion ratio applies, but 100% repatriation is compulsory, and failure to repatriate within the 90-day window without a prior SAFE-approved extension triggers delinquency classification, penalties, and downgrading of the entity's trade facilitation status.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Foreign Exchange Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Deposit Account / RMB Capital Account
General Operational RMB and Foreign Currency Accounts
Working Capital RMB Account / Export Proceeds Collection Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMI cross-border viability is very low for any China-domiciled WFOE lacking a local banking license. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Airwallex or Currenxie cannot act as the primary treasury rail in China because SAFE and PBOC require all capital account transactions, FDI injections, export collections, and profit repatriations to route through domestic banks under the Regulatory Information Sharing platform. No unlicensed foreign EMI is permitted to open domestic yuan accounts or process corporate payments in mainland China; therefore, the WFOE may only use such EMIs for incidental offshore spending outside China, while all onshore compliance flows must remain with tier-1 domestic banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: China requires the legal representative or a duly authorized officer with a notarized power of attorney to appear physically at the bank branch for corporate account opening. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted in practice; senior management and the ultimate beneficial owner must provide original identification documents, board resolutions, and specimen signatures in person. For an offshore legal representative, a Chinese consulate-notarized POA plus a local banker's interview via video conference may be conditionally accepted, but the final call rests with the bank's compliance section and usually requires at least one in-country signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is a non-resident individual with wealth originating outside China and no visible operating history in the target market.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The WFOE must supply the shareholder's certified passport copies, a professional background dossier with employment history, source-of-wealth declaration, audited financial statements of the overseas parent, tax residence certificates, and an organizational chart showing all intermediate holding vehicles up to the natural-person UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection arrives from a third-party offshore jurisdiction not aligned with the parent company's declared corporate seat.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The company must provide the full transaction chain from the remitting account to the ultimate parent, including SWIFT MT103 Incoming Data, a corporate treasury department funding letter, evidence of intra-group loan or equity subscription arrangements, and legal opinions verifying the corporate existence and the authority of signatories in the remitting jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business scope includes cloud document automation and e-signature authentication, which may trigger data localization and indirect cybersecurity licensing concerns under PIPL and Data Security Law.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The WFOE must produce the registered business scope certificate, a written data-flow architecture showing no sensitive personal data is transferred offshore, the official ICP filing, any applicable software and information security registrations, and an external legal audit confirming the entity does not require a payment institution license.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large outbound disbursements to overseas software vendors are frequent and inconsistent with the declared low-risk technology service revenue model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The treasury department must provide board-approved vendor contracts, annual budget forecasts, actual-Service invoices, customs declarations where software is embedded in physical media, social insurance and payroll records proving legitimate local operations, and a self-commissioned audit trail of the procurement and payment workflow.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection must be routed through a designated domestic bank that is SAFE-authorized to process FDI. The WFOE first completes business registration and obtains the Foreign Investment Information Reptization certificate from the local Administration for Market Regulation; then it opens a Foreign Exchange Capital Settlement Account at the chosen tier-1 bank and submits the SAFE FDI registration form. The overseas parent remits the approved share capital via SWIFT MT103 or CHIPS using the proper SAFE purpose code (e.g., 'Foreign Investment capital injection'), and the receiving bank performs a real-time documentary examination of the remittance instruction, the bank's internal FX registration number, the equity subscription agreement, and the board resolution. Upon credit, the bank verifies the capital via the SAFE system, supports capital account payment information, and allows the WFOE to convert funds to RMB through the bank's settlement service; the use of the converted RMB is monitored against the business scope and requires invoices, contracts, and payment applications for each outgoing RMB transaction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade disbursements, the WFOE should primarily use SWIFT MT103 for service payments and licensing fees, supported by contracts and tax withholding proofs; for import of hardware or software media, Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C at sight) are recommended as they provide both payment security and documentary compliance; Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) are secondary rails that reduce bank risk but offer less protection. Each outbound transaction must be reported under the trade in goods or trade in services survey code, with submission of the Foreign Exchange Payment Agreement, customs declarations if goods are involved, and the corresponding SAFE business registration for current account payments; all payments must be processed through the WFOE's domestic settlement bank to maintain a complete regulatory audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB/FX forwards executed through domestic banks under the Enterprise Hedging Framework for current account exposure
Onshore currency swaps transacted by the WFOE with PBOC-approved financial institutions for capital account and balance sheet hedging
Plain vanilla FX options purchased from domestic banks to hedge projected profit repatriation and operational cash flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Publicity Report for Foreign-Invested Enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June covering the preceding calendar year; no extension is available for weekends or public holidays
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-publication by the 30 June deadline results in the WFOE being included in the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operation within 10 working days. If the abnormal listing remains uncorrected for three consecutive years, the WFOE is moved to the List of Seriously Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprises, triggering market-access restrictions, credit punishment, and potential administrative revocation of the business license; false annual report data may also result in fines and director disqualification penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the same SAMR National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System single-report window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June, combined with the enterprise information publicity annual report; no separate filing portal or separate deadline applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or submission of false foreign investment information triggers a MOFCOM rectification order with a 20-working-day cure period. Continued non-compliance can lead to administrative penalties, including a fine exposure of up to RMB 100,000 or other applicable statutory sanctions, plus adverse credit entries that impair future foreign-exchange registration, cross-border financing, and corporate restructuring approvals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Reconciliation and Final Settlement Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through the in-charge tax collection authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May immediately following each calendar tax year ending 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the WFOE to a late-filing fine, escalating up to RMB 10,000 in serious cases, and a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% on overdue corporate income tax. If understated tax is classified as tax evasion, the tax authority may recover the unpaid tax and impose a penalty of 50% to five times the unpaid amount; extreme non-compliance can trigger business license revocation and personal liability for responsible officers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statement Audit by a PRC Licensed CPA Firm
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No standalone regulatory filing is required; the audit report is prepared for the shareholders and board, retained in the statutory corporate records, and used to support the annual corporate income tax settlement and annual enterprise information report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the shareholders meeting that approves the annual financial statements and, as a practical prerequisite, before the 31 May corporate income tax annual settlement deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a Company Law-compliant audited financial report constitutes a corporate governance violation, invalidates the formal shareholder approval process, and exposes directors and senior management to administrative liability. The tax authority may also reject the financial books, estimate taxable income, and impose penalties on any resulting underpayment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: PRC Company Law imposes a mandatory annual audit on every limited-liability company, including a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise, regardless of quantitative balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount thresholds. No size-based exemption applies to a standard WFOE; a CPA firm licensed in China must be appointed to audit the annual financial statements. Audits are performed in accordance with China Standards on Auditing (CSAs). A small-scale entity may use the Simplified Accounting Rules for Small Enterprises for bookkeeping, but this election does not remove the statutory audit obligation for the WFOE.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Enterprise Accounting Standards (CAS) as issued by the Ministry of Finance, substantially converged with IFRS; qualifying small-scale entities may apply the Small Enterprise Accounting Standards (SEAS). Statutory audits are governed by China Standards on Auditing (CSAs). PRC accounting archive rules require accounting books, vouchers, and related records to be retained for at least 30 years, with annual financial reports retained permanently and tax records retained for at least 10 years.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The PRC does not maintain a separate annual UBO declaration. Beneficial ownership, actual controllers, and foreign investor information are disclosed through the combined SAMR/MOFCOM annual report. Any change in shareholders, registered capital, equity transfer, ultimate beneficial owner, or actual controller must be submitted to SAMR for business registration alteration within 30 days of the change and through the MOFCOM foreign investment change report within 30 days. The WFOE must also update its on-site register of shareholders before the shareholding change can be enforced against the company or third parties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Shareholder Register) maintained at the registered address with shareholder names, contribution amounts, shareholding percentages, and update dates.
Register of Directors and Supervisors containing appointment, resignation, and nomination records for directors, supervisors, and senior management.

Register of Charges/Mortgages: not a standalone PRC statutory register; equity pledges and asset security interests are perfected by public registration with SAMR or other applicable authorities, and the WFOE should retain a copy of each registered pledge record on site.
Minute Book containing minutes of shareholders meetings, board meetings, executive resolutions, and written consent resolutions.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 2,500 per annum for registered address leasing and local corporate secretarial support in typical second-tier cities; tier-1 city arrangements may reach USD 4,000 or more.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 4,500 for a single-entity, low-risk LegalTech SaaS WFOE without material intercompany financing or IP transfers; USD 5,000 - USD 12,000 if cross-border service agreements, transfer pricing documentation, or intra-group royalties are present.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises are entitled to a 15% reduced rate. Small and low-profit enterprises with taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million may apply an effective 5% rate. Additional 100% super deduction applies to qualifying research and development expenses. Software enterprises may access a two-year CIT exemption followed by three-year 50% reduced rate. No preferential free-zone tax holiday applies to a Mainland China WFOE absent a specific provincial-level incentive.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form A) and supporting schedules submitted through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing portal, commonly branded as e-Tax@China; quarterly provisional returns are submitted via the same platform.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement combined with quarterly provisional filings during the tax year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional CIT returns must be filed within 15 days after the end of each quarter. The annual return and any final CIT balance must be filed and paid within 5 months after the close of the fiscal year, i.e. by May 31 for a calendar year taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue: gross proceeds from cloud document automation subscriptions, e-signature transaction fees, implementation services, and maintenance contracts, stated exclusive of VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately identify revenue that embeds a license of software or patent rights to a foreign group member; such embedded royalty streams must be allocated on an arm's length basis. Cross-border SaaS marketplace sales generated through foreign platforms must be reflected here and reconciled with VAT export/zero-rating records to avoid under-declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs: direct costs of cloud hosting, data-center capacity, verification and e-signature cryptographic services, and direct labor.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If cloud infrastructure is obtained from a non-resident group entity, expenses are deductible only to the extent supported by valid invoices or equivalent vouchers, executed contracts, and arm's length pricing. A mere recharge or allocation of group overhead with no actual service benefit will be disregarded and treated as a dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and surcharges: urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, local education surcharge, stamp duty, and property tax; VAT and corporate income tax are excluded.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When the WFOE is the withholding agent for non-resident VAT on imported software or services, the VAT and surcharges withheld must be tracked separately, not expensed as a CIT deduction unless the contract makes the WFOE liable. This box should not contain notional taxes levied on foreign counterparties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling expenses: SaaS channel partner commissions, online advertising, business development costs, and trade show expenditures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Commissions or referral fees paid to non-resident agents for services performed outside China are deductible only if commercial substance exists and withholding obligations were settled for any taxable service income connected with China. Payments structured as commissions to a shell foreign affiliate without staff or functions will be recharacterized as non-deductible profit distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative expenses: legal and professional fees, office rent, general management, HR, and qualifying research and development expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: LegalTech R&D activities should be segregated to substantiate the 100% super deduction; an R&D project file including project plan, staffing logs, and cost allocation is required. Administrative fees recharged by a foreign parent must satisfy the benefit test and must not duplicate services already performed by Chinese employees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial expenses: interest on intercompany debt, bank fees, exchange losses, and guarantor fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to a non-resident lender is deductible to the extent of the 2:1 debt-to-equity safe harbor for non-financial enterprises. Excess interest is treated as a deemed dividend subject to 10% WHT, unless treaty relief is available and the lender is the beneficial owner of the interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating profit, non-operating income, non-operating expenses, and total accounting profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-operating items include foreign-exchange gains or losses and government grants. Any related-party waiver of debt or forgiveness of accounts payable may be taxable income and could indicate disguised repatriation to the overseas investor.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: taxable income increase/decrease items, loss carryover offset, preferential tax rate application, foreign tax credits, and final CIT payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Announce transfer pricing adjustments that increase taxable income, non-deductible penalties, and 10% deemed-dividend adjustments for excessive interest or royalty payments. Disclose country-by-country reporting obligations and related-party transaction aggregates on ancillary forms before the annual filing deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual CIT return attracts a penalty of RMB 2,000 up to RMB 10,000 in ordinary cases, increasing to RMB 2,000-50,000 for false or incomplete filing. Late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% of unpaid tax. Tax evasion on reassessment exposes the taxpayer to a fine of 50% to five times the underpaid tax. Deliberate concealment involving criminal thresholds may be prosecuted as tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201 with imprisonment up to seven years; false issuance of special VAT invoices may additionally expose persons responsible to penalties up to life imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate on an outbound dividend, the non-resident corporate shareholder must be the beneficial owner of the dividend and hold the WFOE through a substantive ownership structure. The withholding agent may apply the treaty rate when filing the withholding return after collecting the Tax Residency Certificate issued by the shareholder's residence tax authority, a completed Application for Preferential Tax Treatment under Tax Treaties form, and an updated beneficial ownership self-declaration. The Chinese tax authority may issue a notice requiring supplementary evidence of economic substance before accepting the reduced rate. If the full 10% was withheld, the non-resident shareholder may file a refund claim with the competent Chinese tax authority within three years, attaching the same treaty relief package.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory withholding tax rate is 10% for outbound interest and royalties, and an additional 6% VAT with related surcharges applies to imported royalties/technical services unless zero-rated. DTA rates vary by jurisdiction; by way of example, the China-Hong Kong arrangement before amendment provided a 7% rate on interest and a 5% rate on royalties qualifying for treaty protection and paid to a beneficial owner; other treaties may provide 0%, 5%, 7% or 10% rates depending on the type of income.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when annual related-party tangible-asset transfers exceed RMB 200 million, intangible-asset transfers exceed RMB 100 million, financial-asset transfers exceed RMB 100 million, or related-party service transactions exceed RMB 40 million. Master File preparation is generally triggered when total related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion or where group-level entry conditions in the annual related-party report require consolidated disclosure. Quarterly/annual related-party transaction tables must be filed together with the annual CIT return.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not operate an Economic Substance Regulation modeled on offshore jurisdictions, but the economic-substance doctrine is embedded in the general anti-avoidance rule (Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 47) and the Special Tax Adjustment Measures (State Taxation Administration Announcement 2017 No. 6). The tax authority will disregard a WFOE or contract structure lacking real decision-making, personnel, assets, and risks, and will recharacterize the arrangement based on its commercial substance. For treaty relief, the OECD Beneficial Ownership commentary and China's treaty practice require the income recipient to exercise substantive powers over the income, so a conduit WFOE holding intangible rights without core income-generating activities will lose treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of corporate form and treaty shopping through a substance-less conduit WFOE
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a Mainland China WFOE with no employees, no premises, no decision-making function, and negligible capital, solely to register legal-tech IP, execute back-to-back contracts with end users, and remit residual profits to a low-tax offshore shareholder under a claim that the WFOE is the beneficial owner of royalties or dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits and disallowance of the intermediary company; beneficial owner recharacterization under EIT Law Article 47 and SAT Announcement 2017 No. 6; the tax authority may reconstruct taxable income using a deemed profit margin and impose a fine of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax plus daily late-payment interest at 0.05%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced under the Company Law where the director intentionally uses the company to evade tax and abuses limited liability; directors and actual controllers become jointly liable for the unpaid tax and penalties. Blacklisting through the tax credit reporting system imposes travel restrictions on legal representatives, and egregious, intentional non-payment may trigger criminal liability for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fabricated cost scheme and false invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using fake supplier invoices or staged procurement contracts for software development, cloud services, or consultancy to create artificial deductible costs, reduce the taxable profits of the WFOE, and disguise profit repatriation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 63 of the Tax Administration Law, tax evasion is punished by recovery of the unpaid tax, a late-payment surcharge, and a fine of 50% to five times the tax underpaid. False issuance of special VAT invoices violates Criminal Law Article 205 and may lead to criminal fines, confiscation, and imprisonment up to life for responsible persons in severe cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative, finance director, and tax responsible persons who signed or approved false invoices are personally exposed to criminal prosecution; if the WFOE lacks assets, directors personally compensate the tax authority through asset restitution and freezing orders. Directors also face a personal fine and a statutory ban on serving as directors in any Chinese company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Omission of transfer pricing documentation and cross-border payment disclosures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately failing to prepare the contemporaneous Local File and Master File when related-party transaction thresholds are exceeded, omitting intercompany royalties, interest, or cost-sharing arrangements from the annual related-party transaction schedules, and paying foreign affiliates without any arm's length benchmark or beneficial ownership evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may disregard undisclosed related-party transactions, adjust taxable income by the deemed profit method, and impose the standard understatement penalty of 50%-500% of the adjustment plus daily surcharges. Refusal to produce documentation permits the authority to make a unilateral assessment and accelerates a special audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify false annual related-party disclosures are jointly liable for the resulting tax deficiency under civil recovery procedures; intentional concealment can be prosecuted as tax evasion, leading to confiscation of assets, travel bans, and up to seven years imprisonment depending on the amount evaded.
